subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion categorically reject every existing checkout path, or should OpenClaw offer an explicit high-friction opt-in for adopting an existing checkout?
rationale: Fresh-only conversion closes the reported trust boundary, but it deliberately breaks an established setup path; automation cannot decide whether that compatibility cost or an explicit unsafe override matches updater policy.

options.title: Approve fresh-only conversion
options.body: Require an unused path, retain clear remediation text, and document the intentional compatibility break as the secure updater policy.

options.title: Add explicit adoption override
options.body: Keep fresh-only behavior by default but permit a clearly named, warned, user-requested override that accepts the existing-checkout risk.

options.title: Pause for updater redesign
options.body: Do not change the contract until conversion ownership and recovery are redesigned around the canonical state database.

recommendation.title: Approve fresh-only conversion
recommendation.body: Require an unused path, retain clear remediation text, and document the intentional compatibility break as the secure updater policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the current updater orchestration and recent update-safety changes.
